chapter.name: Vector Algebra
chapter.blurb: Scalars and vectors, the position vector and direction cosines, types of vectors, and the triangle and parallelogram laws of addition. The chapter then works with vectors in component form xi + yj + zk, the section formula, and the two products of vectors: the scalar (dot) product with projections, and the vector (cross) product with areas of triangles and parallelograms.

scope_in.item: Classify quantities as scalars (magnitude only) or vectors (magnitude and direction), and describe a vector as a directed line segment with initial point, terminal point and magnitude |AB|
Write the position vector OP of P(x, y, z) and find its magnitude sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
Find direction angles, direction cosines l = x/r, m = y/r, n = z/r and direction ratios of a vector, using l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1 (while a^2 + b^2 + c^2 need not be 1)
Recognise zero, unit, coinitial, collinear, equal and negative vectors, and free vectors, including in figures such as a square or parallelogram

Add vectors by the triangle law and parallelogram law, use the zero resultant of a triangle's sides taken in order, form a - b = a + (-b), and use the commutative, associative and additive identity properties
Multiply a vector by a scalar (|lambda a| = |lambda| |a|, direction same or opposite by the sign of lambda), and form the unit vector (1/|a|) a and a vector of given magnitude in a given direction

Write vectors in component form xi + yj + zk; find magnitude, sum, difference, scalar multiples and equality in components; test collinearity by proportional components; write unit vectors in the XY-plane as cos theta i + sin theta j
Find the vector joining two points P1P2 = (x2 - x1)i + (y2 - y1)j + (z2 - z1)k and its magnitude
Use the section formula for internal division (mb + na)/(m + n), external division (mb - na)/(m - n) and the midpoint (a + b)/2; show three points are collinear and find the ratio of division

Define and compute the scalar product a . b = |a||b| cos theta = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3, use i . i = 1, i . j = 0, the perpendicularity test, commutativity and distributivity, and find the angle between two vectors
Find the projection of a vector on a directed line or on another vector, (a . b)/|b|, and use a . a = |a|^2 to find quantities such as |a - b| and |a + b + c|

Define and compute the vector product a x b = |a||b| sin theta n (right handed system), use i x j = k, j x i = -k, b x a = -(a x b), a x b = 0 for parallel vectors, distributivity, and the determinant form in components
Find a unit vector perpendicular to two given vectors, sin theta = |a x b|/(|a||b|), and the areas of a triangle (1/2)|a x b| and a parallelogram |a x b|

concepts.name: Scalars, vectors, position vector and direction cosines
concepts.description: Distinguishing scalar and vector quantities, the directed line segment with initial and terminal points and magnitude, the position vector of P(x, y, z) and its magnitude, and the direction angles, direction cosines (l, m, n) and direction ratios (a, b, c) of a vector.
concepts.idea: A scalar has only magnitude; a vector has magnitude and direction, drawn as a directed line segment. The position vector of a point P is the vector from the origin O to P.
concepts.rule: For P(x, y, z) with r = |OP| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2), the direction cosines are l = x/r, m = y/r, n = z/r and l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1; the direction ratios a, b, c are any numbers proportional to l, m, n, and a^2 + b^2 + c^2 need not be 1.
concepts.example: For P(2, 3, 6), r = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = 7, so the direction cosines of OP are 2/7, 3/7, 6/7 and 2, 3, 6 are its direction ratios.

questions.q: A student says that 2, 3, 6 are the direction cosines of the position vector of P(2, 3, 6). Is the student right? Justify.
questions.a: No. 2^2 + 3^2 + 6^2 = 49, not 1, so 2, 3, 6 cannot be direction cosines; they are direction ratios. Dividing by r = 7 gives the direction cosines 2/7, 3/7, 6/7.
s: Shows 4 + 9 + 36 = 49 is not 1, so these are direction ratios, not direction cosines

s: Gives a valid point with non-zero integer coordinates and magnitude 9
Writes its direction cosines
Verifies the sum of squares is 1

concepts.name: Types of vectors
concepts.description: Zero (null), unit, coinitial, collinear, equal and negative vectors, and free vectors, identified in figures such as a square or parallelogram.
concepts.idea: Vectors are classified by their magnitude, their direction and their initial points; in this chapter all vectors are free, so they may be moved parallel to themselves.
concepts.rule: Equal vectors have the same magnitude and direction (initial points may differ); collinear vectors are parallel to the same line whatever their magnitudes and directions; the negative of AB is BA; a zero vector has zero magnitude and no definite direction.
concepts.example: In a square ABCD, vector AB = vector DC (equal), AB and CD are collinear but not equal, and AB and AD are coinitial.

concepts.name: Addition and subtraction of vectors
concepts.description: The triangle law and parallelogram law of vector addition, the zero resultant of the sides of a triangle taken in order, the difference a - b = a + (-b), and the commutative, associative and additive identity properties.
concepts.idea: Adding vectors means following one displacement after another: place the initial point of the second at the terminal point of the first.
concepts.rule: Triangle law: vector AB + vector BC = vector AC. Parallelogram law: the sum of two adjacent sides is the diagonal through their common point. a + b = b + a, (a + b) + c = a + (b + c), a + 0 = a, a + (-a) = 0, and a - b = a + (-b).
concepts.example: In triangle ABC, vector AB + vector BC + vector CA = 0, because the sides taken in order bring you back to the starting point.

questions.q: A student writes: 'In triangle ABC, vector AB + vector BC = vector CA.' Identify the error and correct it.
questions.a: The error is the direction of the resultant. By the triangle law, AB + BC = AC (from the start A to the end C). Vector CA = -AC, so the correct statement is AB + BC = AC, equivalently AB + BC + CA = 0.

Writes AB + BC = AC (or AB + BC + CA = 0)

questions.q: Construct a closed path of four displacements on a quadrilateral PQRS and show, using the triangle law step by step, that their vector sum is the zero vector.
questions.a: Take PQ, QR, RS, SP. By the triangle law PQ + QR = PR, then PR + RS = PS, and PS + SP = PS + (-PS) = 0. So PQ + QR + RS + SP = 0.
s: Combines PQ + QR = PR

concepts.name: Scalar multiple, component form and unit vectors
concepts.description: Multiplying a vector by a scalar, the unit vectors i, j, k, the component form xi + yj + zk with its magnitude, sum, difference, equality and scalar multiples in components, collinearity by proportional components, unit vectors in a given direction, and direction cosines from components.
concepts.idea: Every vector in space can be written as xi + yj + zk; the scalar components x, y, z are its direction ratios, and all vector operations reduce to working on components.
concepts.rule: |lambda a| = |lambda| |a| and lambda a is collinear with a. If a = a1 i + a2 j + a3 k then |a| = sqrt(a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2), the unit vector along a is (1/|a|) a, and b is collinear with a if and only if b1/a1 = b2/a2 = b3/a3 = lambda.
concepts.example: For a = 2i + 3j + k, |a| = sqrt(14), so the unit vector along a is (2i + 3j + k)/sqrt(14).

concepts.name: Vector joining two points and section formula
concepts.description: The vector P1P2 = (x2 - x1)i + (y2 - y1)j + (z2 - z1)k and its magnitude, the position vector of a point dividing a segment internally or externally in the ratio m : n, the midpoint, and showing three points collinear.
concepts.idea: The vector from P to Q is the position vector of Q minus the position vector of P; the section formula weights each end by the part of the ratio next to the other end.
concepts.rule: Vector PQ = OQ - OP. If P, Q have position vectors a, b then R dividing PQ internally in m : n has position vector (mb + na)/(m + n), externally (mb - na)/(m - n), and the midpoint is (a + b)/2.
concepts.example: The vector from P(2, 3, 0) to Q(-1, -2, -4) is -3i - 5j - 4k; the midpoint of P(2, 3, 4) and Q(4, 1, -2) is 3i + 2j + k.

concepts.name: Scalar (dot) product and projection
concepts.description: The scalar product a . b = |a||b| cos theta, its observations (perpendicularity, i . i = 1, i . j = 0, angle between vectors), commutativity and distributivity, the component formula a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3, the projection of a vector on a line or on another vector, and uses such as finding |a - b| and testing perpendicularity.
concepts.idea: The dot product measures how much two vectors point the same way; it is a number, positive for an acute angle, zero for perpendicular vectors and negative for an obtuse angle.
concepts.rule: a . b = |a||b| cos theta = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3, so cos theta = (a . b)/(|a||b|). For nonzero vectors, a . b = 0 if and only if a is perpendicular to b. The projection of a on b is (a . b)/|b|, and a . a = |a|^2.
concepts.example: For a = i + j - k and b = i - j + k, a . b = 1 - 1 - 1 = -1 and |a| = |b| = sqrt(3), so cos theta = -1/3.

concepts.name: Vector (cross) product and area
concepts.description: The vector product a x b = |a||b| sin theta n with the right handed rule, its observations (parallel vectors give the zero vector, i x j = k, j x i = -k, not commutative), distributivity, the determinant form in components, unit vectors perpendicular to two vectors, sin theta from the cross product, and areas of triangles and parallelograms.
concepts.idea: The cross product of two vectors is a new vector perpendicular to both, whose length equals the area of the parallelogram they span.
concepts.rule: a x b = |a||b| sin theta n, with a, b, n right handed; b x a = -(a x b); a x b = 0 for nonzero vectors if and only if they are parallel. In components a x b = (a2 b3 - a3 b2)i - (a1 b3 - a3 b1)j + (a1 b2 - a2 b1)k. Area of parallelogram = |a x b|, area of triangle = (1/2)|a x b|.
